chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked him about sleeping after the morning prayer, and he said: Indeed, rizq is spread out during that hour, so I dislike that a man should sleep during that hour.

And al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: The sleep of early morning is ill-omened; it drives away rizq, yellows the complexion, makes it ugly, and alters it. It is the sleep of every ill-fated one. Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, apportions sustenance between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun.

key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: sustenance or livelihood apportioned by Allah
key_terms.النَّوْمِ: sleep, especially sleep taken after the morning prayer
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the early morning period after dawn prayer

ai.seo_question: Why is sleeping after the morning prayer considered disliked in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discourages sleeping after salat al-ghadāh, describing that time as a period in which rizq is distributed. It presents wakefulness in the early morning as connected to blessing, livelihood, and good condition, while portraying sleep then as blameworthy and harmful.
